newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee regions to see rain, seasonal temps.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee regions to see rain, seasonal temps.

text.p: Isolated rain showers are forecast to reach Brazil's key coffee growing regions in the north of Sao Paulo and Minas Gerais states toward the second half of this week, independent meteorologists Somar said.

Temperatures should remain normal for the time of year, with minimum levels of between 13 and 17 degrees Celsius and no threat of temperatures falling to critical levels over the next eight days, it added.
The approach of the Brazilian winter brings with it the threat of frost damage to the country's coffee trees.

According to some records, the earliest frost in the last 100 years to hit the coffee regions was on May 31 but the most critical months are June and July. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
